3. **`active_plan_and_acceptance`**: Governed by [`docs/raisa-provider-free-read-only-arrival-check-in-command-family-convergence-review-plan.md`](file:///C:/Users/sarashera/EMR4-worktrees/arrival-check-in-convergence-3bed3eb3/docs/raisa-provider-free-read-only-arrival-check-in-command-family-convergence-review-plan.md), [`docs/security/raisa-provider-free-read-only-arrival-check-in-command-family-convergence-review-threat-model-delta.md`](file:///C:/Users/sarashera/EMR4-worktrees/arrival-check-in-convergence-3bed3eb3/docs/security/raisa-provider-free-read-only-arrival-check-in-command-family-convergence-review-threat-model-delta.md), [`docs/raisa-provider-free-read-only-arrival-check-in-command-family-convergence-review.md`](file:///C:/Users/sarashera/EMR4-worktrees/arrival-check-in-convergence-3bed3eb3/docs/raisa-provider-free-read-only-arrival-check-in-command-family-convergence-review.md), and parent orientation [`docs/raisa-provider-free-read-only-post-cancellation-programme-orientation.md`](file:///C:/Users/sarashera/EMR4-worktrees/arrival-check-in-convergence-3bed3eb3/docs/raisa-provider-free-read-only-post-cancellation-programme-orientation.md).

---

## 2. Review Question Assessment

**Core Finding:**
Exact source evidence completely supports the decision that dedicated check-in—not generic state assignment—is the future canonical product-facing arrival command. General status is properly retained for other appointment lifecycle transitions, and its ordinary product-facing `Arrived` target will be removed during a later atomic two-client cutover. The reusable deterministic kernel is clearly decoupled from Rayleen-named default-off admission scaffolding without widening present authority or opening unreviewed surfaces.

---

## 3. Detailed Responses to Required Challenges

1. **Exact Worktree, Branch, HEAD, and Diff Inventory:**
   - Pre-review and post-review `git status --short --branch` confirmed clean state on `codex/review-arrival-check-in-convergence-3bed3eb3`.
   - HEAD confirmed as exact `3bed3eb32dd1b8723bf5aa6218963b757ebc0e3d`.
   - Baseline diff against `fb39d235c5dc4de2440a5b0e4685ee5da5b4f4d0` contains strictly allowlisted review, threat-model, plan, test, error register, and orchestration receipt files. No product source, API schemas, migrations, or frontend JS files were modified.

2. **Generic Status vs. A5.1 Semantic Divergence:**
   - Both pathways can update the database column `Appointment.status` to `AppointmentStatus.Arrived`, but they represent fundamentally different domain contracts.
   - *Generic status* admits broad roles (`Receptionist`, `GP`, `Nurse`, `Admin`, `PracticeOwner`), permits any valid non-terminal transition to `Arrived`, uses general status confirmation evidence, handles waiting areas via general clear/assign heuristics without same-location validation, and emits no dedicated domain check-in event.
   - *A5.1 check-in* enforces `UserRole.Receptionist` authority, strictly requires source status `Booked` or `Confirmed`, consumes single-use HMAC evidence with durable hash claims preventing replay under different keys, enforces active same-practice same-location waiting-area compatibility, and atomically writes status, audit log, and the dedicated `diary.appointment_checked_in.v1` committed event.

3. **Check-In as a Domain Command vs. Bare State Synonym:**
   - Setting `status = Arrived` is merely an attribute mutation. Check-in is a distinct General Practice operational domain event certifying physical/telehealth arrival by authorised front-desk staff, recording point-in-time evidence, assigning compatible waiting facilities, and publishing downstream event notifications. Treating check-in as synonymous with general status mutation would make audit/event completeness depend arbitrarily on client selection.

4. **A5.1 Exact Rules and Replay Invariants:**
   - Confirmed in [`app/routers/appointments.py`](file:///C:/Users/sarashera/EMR4-worktrees/arrival-check-in-convergence-3bed3eb3/app/routers/appointments.py#L3217-L3450):
     - Role restriction: `require_role(UserRole.Receptionist)`.
     - State validation: Source must be `Booked` or `Confirmed`; `already_arrived` and invalid source statuses block execution.
     - Confirmation evidence: Cryptographic HMAC token with strict TTL; SHA-256 evidence hash recorded via `claim_appointment_check_in_command`.
     - Waiting-area validation: Validates same practice, active status, non-null appointment location parity; preserves existing area if omitted/null; rejects moves/removals.
     - Atomicity: Status update, audit log with evidence audit codes, `record_appointment_checked_in_event`, and private receipt committed in one locked transaction.
     - Replay: Exact same-key replay returns stored JSON; reuse of the same signed evidence token under a different idempotency key is rejected with HTTP 409 `confirmation_replay_rejected`.

5. **Reusable Kernel vs. A5.1 Scaffolding:**
   - The review explicitly separates the core domain logic (transition rules, role policy, row locking, evidence hash consumption, waiting-area validation, audit/event composition, bounded readback) from A5.1 development scaffolding (`rayleen_a5_check_in_enabled`, `rayleen_a5_check_in_synthetic_practice_ids`, Rayleen naming, authored-synthetic claim boundary). Present authority remains completely closed and default-off.

6. **Future Atomic Two-Client Cutover Rule:**
   - To eliminate split-brain write semantics and avoid transitional dead zones, both first-party clients (ordinary Diary in [`docs/diary/diary.js`](file:///C:/Users/sarashera/EMR4-worktrees/arrival-check-in-convergence-3bed3eb3/docs/diary/diary.js) and Reception One in [`docs/diary/meta-grid.js`](file:///C:/Users/sarashera/EMR4-worktrees/arrival-check-in-convergence-3bed3eb3/docs/diary/meta-grid.js)) must migrate to the dedicated check-in command simultaneously with closing ordinary product-facing `Arrived` admission in generic status.

7. **Waiting-Area Movement/Removal Boundary:**
   - Check-in allows optional initial assignment or preservation of an existing valid waiting area. Moving to another area or removing an assigned area remains a distinct domain operation (`waiting_area_move`) that is not silently admitted by check-in.

8. **Static Grammar and Route-Contract Classifications:**
   - [`app/services/diary/action_grammar.py`](file:///C:/Users/sarashera/EMR4-worktrees/arrival-check-in-convergence-3bed3eb3/app/services/diary/action_grammar.py): `check_in` as `implemented=False` is *scope-qualified current* (no generally admitted product action exists); prose stating "no signed endpoint exists" is *factually superseded* by the mounted A5.1 confirm endpoint.
   - [`app/services/diary/action_route_contract.py`](file:///C:/Users/sarashera/EMR4-worktrees/arrival-check-in-convergence-3bed3eb3/app/services/diary/action_route_contract.py): `planned_not_implemented` is *scope-qualified current*; notes regarding "no confirm action" are *superseded/incomplete* route inventory.
   - [`app/services/diary/confirm_actions.py`](file:///C:/Users/sarashera/EMR4-worktrees/arrival-check-in-convergence-3bed3eb3/app/services/diary/confirm_actions.py): Lacks `DiaryConfirmAction.check_in` because check-in is not yet admitted for general product use.
   - Static files are appropriately left untouched in this read-only review tranche.

9. **Narrowest Successor Definition:**
   - Successor tranche `raisa-provider-free-unmounted-canonical-check-in-product-adapter-extraction-rehearsal` is bounded to extracting the unmounted reusable check-in product adapter with authored-synthetic unit tests. It opens no routes, changes no flags, enables no practices, modifies no UI, and accesses no product/provider data.

10. **Register Incidents AER-0405 through AER-0412:**
    - AER-0405 (prose fixture whitespace normalization), AER-0406 (asymmetric peer link validation), AER-0407 (population fixture updates), AER-0408 (residual recurring-pattern assertion separation), AER-0409 (five-field recurrence composite vs signature text), AER-0410 (residual-list filter/exclusion set pairing), AER-0411 (Current Baton compact live row historical name fixture drift), and AER-0412 (test prose assertion mismatch on "current bounded-chain endpoints") accurately capture test harness fixture failures and corrections while preserving the underlying review candidate and product codebase.

11. **Manifest Command Execution:**
    - All commands C01–C07 executed in exact order with exit code 0. HEAD and worktree remain clean and unmodified.

The arrival/check-in convergence review is complete, mathematically and architecturally sound, and rigorously verified against the codebase. No P0–P2 findings, source misstatements, or unsafe successor boundaries exist.
